title: Today's feel: head pressure eases a notch.
caption: Today's feel: head pressure eases a notch. With quiet conditions and no recent solar bursts, some people notice less fullness behind the eyes and temples. If your head still feels touchy, local weather—pressure swings, humidity, wind, or allergens—can play a big role, so check what’s moving through your area before you blame the sky. — Kp 2.7 • Bz -4.7 nT • Schumann 7.69 Hz (snapshot at write time)
snapshot: Geomagnetic activity is quiet. Solar wind is in a normal range and the field is only slightly south-leaning. No flares were recorded and no eruptions were reported. Overall, a steady backdrop.
affects: A steadier backdrop can make it easier to exhale, think a bit more clearly, and hold attention in shorter stretches. Some may still notice leftover edge or heaviness from recent days. Local swings like storms, wind, heat, smoke, or allergens can add their own load, so patterns can vary by location.
playbook:
- Pick one or two light priorities
- Take short outside breaks and move gently
- Keep caffeine earlier in the day
- Drink water and eat on time
- Check local pressure, heat, storms, or AQI
